feedback.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(y)$ has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=-5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-2.$ Find $P(y).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${y}_{1}={y}_{2}=-5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=-2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(y-{y}_{1})^{2} & =(-2){(y-(-5))}^{2} \\  & =(-2){(y+5)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2){(y+5)}^{2} & =(-2)({y}^{2}+10y+25) \\  & =-2{y}^{2}-20y-50.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(y)=-2{y}^{2}-20y-50.$
